ei.title: Chapter 0-QN21 2번: The Personal Diary and Modern Subjectivity
ei.subject: 올림포스9대변별유형

fullPassage: Coming of age in the 18th and 19th centuries, the personal diary became a centerpiece in the construction of a modern subjectivity, at the heart of which is the application of reason and critique to the understanding of world and self, which allowed the creation of a new kind of knowledge. Diaries were central media through which enlightened and free subjects could be constructed. They provided a space where one could write daily about her whereabouts, feelings, and thoughts. Over time and with rereading, disparate entries, events, and happenstances could be rendered into insights and narratives about the self, and allowed for the formation of subjectivity. It is in that context that the idea of "the self [as] both made and explored with words" emerges. Diaries were personal and private; one would write for oneself, or, in Habermas's formulation, one would make oneself public to oneself. By making the self public in a private sphere, the self also became an object for self-inspection and self-critique.

questions.passage: Coming of age in the 18th and 19th centuries, the personal diary became a centerpiece in the (A)[destruction / construction] of a modern subjectivity, at the heart of which is the application of reason and critique to the understanding of world and self, which allowed the creation of a new kind of knowledge. Diaries were (B)[central / marginal] media through which enlightened and free subjects could be constructed. They provided a space where one could write daily about her whereabouts, feelings, and thoughts. Over time and with rereading, disparate entries, events, and happenstances could be rendered into insights and narratives about the self, and allowed for the formation of subjectivity. It is in that context that the idea of "the self [as] both made and explored with words" emerges. Diaries were personal and (C)[public / private]; one would write for oneself, or, in Habermas's formulation, one would make oneself public to oneself. By making the self public in a private sphere, the self also became an object for self-inspection and self-critique.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 일기는 현대적 주체성의 '구성'에서 '중심적' 매체였고, 개인적이고 '사적인' 기록이었다.
det.analysis:
① destruction(파괴) — central — private: (A) 원문은 construction(구성). 일기가 주체성의 '파괴'라는 것은 부적절 ❌
② construction — central — private: 세 자리 모두 원문 일치 ←정답 ✅
③ construction — marginal(주변적) — private: (B) 원문은 central(중심적) ❌
④ construction — central — public(공적): (C) 원문은 private(사적) ❌
det.tip: construction(구성) ↔ destruction(파괴), central(중심적) ↔ marginal(주변적), private(사적) ↔ public(공적)

questions.passage: Coming of age in the 18th and 19th centuries, the personal diary became a centerpiece in the construction of a modern subjectivity, at the heart of which is the application of reason and critique to the understanding of world and self, which allowed the creation of a new kind of knowledge. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: '계몽된' 주체, 서로 다른(이질적인) 기록들, 그리고 자아라는 관념이 '드러난다'.
det.analysis:
① ignorant(무지한) — disparate — emerges: (A) 원문은 enlightened(계몽된) ❌
② enlightened — identical(동일한) — emerges: (B) 원문은 disparate(이질적인) ❌
③ enlightened — disparate — emerges: 세 자리 원문 일치 ←정답 ✅
④ enlightened — disparate — vanishes(사라지다): (C) 원문은 emerges(나타나다) ❌
det.tip: enlightened(계몽된) ↔ ignorant(무지한), disparate(이질적인) ↔ identical(동일한), emerge(나타나다) ↔ vanish(사라지다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a careful and detailed evaluation or judgment of a piece of work or an idea"

det.analysis:
① critique(비평): 어떤 작품이나 생각을 세심하고 상세히 평가·판단하는 것 — 정의 일치 ←정답 ✅
② applause(박수): 칭찬의 표현이지 평가가 아님 ❌
③ imitation(모방): 따라 하는 것 ❌
④ rehearsal(예행연습): 연습이지 평가 아님 ❌
det.tip: critique = 비평, 비판적 평가 (a detailed evaluation)

questions.passage: Diaries were personal and private; one would write for oneself, or, in Habermas's formulation, one would make oneself public to oneself. By __________ (make) the self public in a private sphere, the self also became an object for self-inspection and self-critique.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 전치사 By 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 함. make → making. 'By making the self public'(자아를 공적으로 만듦으로써). 전치사의 목적어는 동명사만 가능하므로 형태가 하나로 결정됨.
det.tip: 전치사(By) + 동명사(-ing). make → making

questions.passage: It is in that context that the idea of "the self [as] both made and explored with words" emerges. Diaries were personal and __________ (privacy); one would write for oneself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 'personal and ___' 자리에는 형용사 personal과 병렬을 이루는 형용사가 와야 함. privacy(명사) → private(형용사). 'personal and private'(개인적이고 사적인). 명사·부사가 아니라 형용사만 성립하므로 형태가 하나로 결정됨.
det.tip: privacy(n. 사생활) → private(adj. 사적인)

questions.passage: Coming of age in the 18th and 19th centuries, the personal diary became a centerpiece in the construction of a modern subjectivity, at the heart of which is the application of reason and critique to the understanding of world and self, which allowed the creation of a new kind of knowledge. Diaries were central media through which enlightened and free subjects could be constructed. They provided a space where one could write daily about her whereabouts, feelings, and thoughts. Over time and with rereading, disparate entries, events, and happenstances could be rendered into insights and narratives about the self, and allowed for the formation of subjectivity. It is in that context that the idea of "the self [as] both made and explored with words" emerges. Diaries were personal and private; one would write __________, or, in Habermas's formulation, one would make oneself public to oneself. By making the self public in a private sphere, the self also became an object for self-inspection and self-critique.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① for others(타인을 위해): 일기는 개인적·사적이므로 타인을 위한 것이 아님 ❌
② for oneself(자기 자신을 위해): 일기는 사적이어서 자기 자신을 위해 씀 ←정답 ✅
③ in public(공개적으로): 사적 기록과 반대 ❌
④ for money(돈을 위해): 문맥과 무관 ❌
det.tip: personal and private → one would write for oneself (자기 자신을 위해)

questions.passage: Coming of age in the 18th and 19th centuries, the personal diary became a centerpiece in the construction of a modern subjectivity, at the heart of which is the application of reason and critique to the understanding of world and self, which allowed the creation of a new kind of knowledge. Diaries were central media through which enlightened and free subjects could be constructed. They provided a space where one could write daily about her whereabouts, feelings, and thoughts. Over time and with rereading, disparate entries, events, and happenstances could be rendered into insights and narratives about the self, and allowed for the formation of subjectivity. It is in that context that the idea of "the self [as] both made and explored with words" emerges. Diaries were personal and private; one would write for oneself, or, in Habermas's formulation, one would make oneself public to oneself. By making the self public in a private sphere, the self also became an object for __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① social recognition and public fame(사회적 인정과 명성): 사적 영역의 자기 응시와 무관 ❌
② economic profit and material gain(경제적 이익): 문맥과 무관 ❌
③ political debate and open protest(정치적 논쟁): 사적 성찰과 반대 ❌
④ self-inspection and self-critique(자기 성찰과 자기비판): 사적 영역에서 자아를 공적으로 만들어 성찰의 대상으로 삼음 ←정답 ✅
det.tip: private sphere → the self as an object for self-inspection and self-critique
